ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The graph shows the variation of boiling point with Group number for the hydrogen compounds of the four lightest members of Group 15 on the periodic table ($NH3$, $PH3$, $AsH3$ and $SbH3$). What is the reason that the lightest member of Group 15 does not follow the trend of the other members, which show that the boiling point decreases with decreasing atomic mass of the Group 15 element?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a line graph, with the legend labeled “Group 15”; the vertical axis represents boiling point, with tick marks from close to 0 to about -100. Among the four square data points, the leftmost point is at about -33, the second point is at about -88, the third point is at about -62, and the rightmost point is at about -18. That is to say, for the heavier Group 15 hydrides PH3, AsH3, and SbH3, the boiling point increases as atomic mass increases, while the boiling point of the lightest NH3 is much higher than the value that should be obtained by extrapolating according to this trend. Reasoning: An increase in boiling point indicates stronger intermolecular forces. PH3, AsH3, and SbH3 are mainly controlled by weaker van der Waals forces/polarizability trends, while in NH3 the N-H bond is strongly polar, the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons, and effective hydrogen bonds can form between NH3 molecules. Hydrogen bonding significantly strengthens intermolecular attraction, so the boiling point of NH3 is anomalously high and deviates from the trend of the other members.

raw_record.question_text: The graph shows the variation of boiling point with Group number for the hydrogen compounds of the four lightest members of Group 15 on the periodic table ($NH3$, $PH3$, $AsH3$ and $SbH3$). What is the reason that the lightest member of Group 15 does not follow the trend of the other members, which show that the boiling point decreases with decreasing atomic mass of the Group 15 element?

method.method_draft: First describe the chart: the three heavier Group 15 hydrides follow a mass/polarizability trend, but the NH3 point is anomalously high for the lightest member. Then use the rule that stronger intermolecular forces increase boiling point. Since NH3 molecules can form hydrogen bonds whereas PH3, AsH3, and SbH3 cannot do so effectively, identify hydrogen bonding as the cause of the deviation.
